mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: High unemployment rates (above 7.0%) signal a weak labor market that suppresses consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 7.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in new housing starts below 500.0 thousand units signals a contraction in the housing sector, which is a key component of consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST falls below 500.0 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the year-over-year CPI (CPIAUCSL) below 1.0% indicates deflationary pressure, which increases the real burden of debt and reduces corporate profit margins, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL growth rate is below 1.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in new housing starts (HOUST) and non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a broad-based economic contraction in both the housing sector and the labor market, which amplifies negative sentiment and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and PAYEMS decline (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of a falling federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates an active monetary policy response to a deteriorating labor market, which typically precedes a bear market in equities, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary easing amid labor market deterioration
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS falls and UNRATE rises (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: In a recessionary regime (defined by GDP contraction), a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 signals a worsening manufacturing sector, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when GDPC1 is contracting (quarterly decline), S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO falls below 100.0 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (defined by strong GDP growth), a decline in quarterly real GDP (GDPC1) below 1.0% annualized growth rate signals an imminent economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods of late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 growth > 2.0% annually), S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 growth falls below 1.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).
